::: {#exm-cartesian-cancel}
#### Why $C$ must not be empty

The condition $C \ne \emptyset$ in @thm-cartesian-cancel is needed.
Let $A = \set{1}$, $B = \set{2}$ and $C = \emptyset$.
A pair in $A \times C$ would need a second entry in $C$, and $C$ has none,
so $A \times C = \emptyset$, and likewise $B \times C = \emptyset$.
So $A \times C = B \times C$, but $A \ne B$.

The proof uses the condition in its first step, to find an element $c \in C$.

:::
